purpose: Defines the minimum machine-checkable product-story and product-acceptance-criterion traceability contract for a future Dopis backlog. It does not create stories or acceptance criteria and does not grant implementation authority.

rules: A story represents one coherent actor-visible product outcome derived from exactly one accepted use case; it is a planning decomposition, not a new requirement or implementation task.
The story actor is linked by its parent use case, and every parent scenario belongs to that use case.
Every story has at least one BEHAVIOR requirement link; each requirement link resolves and exactly matches a parent-use-case link by identifier and role.
Dependencies resolve to other stories, are not self-referential, are acyclic, and express behavioral planning dependency only.
Every populated story has at least one product acceptance criterion.
Context, event, and expected outcomes are the Given-, When-, and Then-equivalents of observable product behavior or business outcomes.
Requirement identifiers resolve and are a subset of their parent story requirement links.
Acceptance criteria do not prescribe APIs, classes, database structure, deployment topology, framework choice, architecture, or test implementation.

future_node_indexes.stories: DOPIS_TRACEABILITY_MATRIX.json future_nodes.stories is an exact validator-recomputed index of backlog story IDs.
future_node_indexes.acceptance_criteria: DOPIS_TRACEABILITY_MATRIX.json future_nodes.acceptance_criteria is an exact validator-recomputed index of backlog acceptance-criterion IDs.
